[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🫂Ministries Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The ministries module contains features related to functions and specific ministries of the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w8oEjl0tNc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🗓️Functions", "col": 12}}, {"id": "riOh9J0you", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church functions are used to track attendance and for linking to other documents.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6k3AeERCdQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating a function, note the following:
- Default function types are provided, but additional function types can be created.
    - When creating a function type, you can choose an existing function as a 'template function'. This will allow you to click the 'Fill From Template' button when creating this type of function in the future to fill in most of the function details using the template function's values. Set the function's Start Date first: the schedule moves to that date and keeps its times.
- Other documents can be linked as items in the function's schedule (i.e. Songs, Sermons, People, Bible References, etc)
- Attendance can be tracked (Additional attendance types can be added if needed)
    - To pre-populate attendance for a function, you can select a 'template function' in the related function type. Then clicking the 'Fill From Template' button will pre-populate all attendance records from the template function.
- 'Headcount' is the number of people in the room, named or not. See Headcount under Check-In Station.
- To publish a function to the public website, check the 'Publish' checkbox. A published function that lasts more than one day shows on the public calendar on each day from its Start Date to its End Date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fn-plan-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Service plan. Plan the order of a service in the Schedule table of the function. Tick Header on a row to make it a heading that starts a part of the service, such as Worship or Response. The bulletin prints a header row as a heading.
- For a song, select the Arrangement and the Key. When you leave the Key empty, Churchit uses the key of the arrangement, else the default key of the song. When you change the song or the arrangement and leave the Key as it was, Churchit sets the key again.
- An arrangement name that the song does not have stops the save. You can only add a song that you can open.
- Displayed (ticked by default) and Printed tell how the words of a song were copied. Tick Streamed or Recorded on the function when the service went out live or was recorded. The Song Usage report counts these uses for CCLI.
- Team Notes are only for the people who serve. They see them on the Ministry Team page. The bulletin never prints them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fn-link-only-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Link Only. Tick Link Only under Publish to keep a published function off the Calendar page, the calendar feed, the home page and the list on the Register page. To show the function, share the link https://<your site>/calendar?event=<function ID>, for example /calendar?event=FUNC-0042. A Register link with ?function=<function ID> works too. Function IDs are numbers in order, so a person can guess the link. Do not use Link Only to keep a private event secret.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fn-meeting-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Online Meeting Link. Add an https link to join the function online, for example a video call. When the function is published, everyone sees Join online on the Calendar page, and the link is in the calendar feed. The link is also in the calendar of the Ministry Team page and in the calendar file of a sign-up. Churchit refuses a link that does not start with https:// or that has a space in it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fn-live-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Streamed. Tick Streamed on a function that you stream live. When the church of the function, or a church above it, has a Live Stream Link on its Church record, the public Calendar page shows Watch live on the function from 15 minutes before it starts until it ends. The button opens the /live page of that church. The Website manual explains the /live page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fn-calendar-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On the public Calendar page, a visitor clicks a published function to see its details: the time, the address with an Open map link, the rooms of its approved Room Bookings, Join online when it has an Online Meeting Link, and Watch live while a streamed function runs. When the address has a map position, a small map shows a pin. Churchit finds the position when the address is saved, if the address lookup is on. A booking that waits for approval or that was denied does not show. With more than one published church, the page of a church that has published branch churches shows Include branch churches. Tick it to also show the functions of those branches, each with its church. The Website manual explains the Subscribe and Download .ics buttons.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "att-count-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Attendance Total. Only Confirmed, Assumed and Checked-In rows count. Signed-Up and Absent rows do not count in the total, in the reports or on the dashboard. A function counts its attendance only from its Start Date. You can add rows before the function, for example from a roster, but its Attendance Total stays 0 until the day of the function. Each day, Churchit updates the totals of the functions of the last week.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "att-write-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who changes an attendance row. A check-in, a sign-up and a member's change on the portal Attendance page each change only that person's row on the Function. A sign-up never replaces a row that says more, such as Checked-In, Confirmed or Absent. If someone checks a person in while you have the Function open, your save stops and asks you to reload the form, so no row is lost.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_0iXv3IWcn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Ministries workspace includes links to function and attendance reports.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "grp-report-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Group filter. The Church Attendance, Function Attendance by Type and Function Attendance by Person reports have a Group filter and a Group column. Choose a group to see only the attendance at the meetings of that group. Leave it empty to see every function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TvoZni0RtF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Hint: in the Function list view, change the view type to 'Calendar' to view the Functions on a calendar.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "att-portal-h3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📋Attendance in the Portal", "col": 12}}, {"id": "att-portal-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members can see their own attendance on the Attendance page of the portal. It lists every function that has them in its attendance, newest first, with their attendance type (for example Checked-In or Signed-Up).
- Functions dated after today are not shown. A recurring function copies its attendance roster onto its occurrences weeks before they happen, so those rows are not yet a record of who came.
- To let members correct their own attendance, tick Members Can Change Their Attendance in Portal Settings. Each row then offers Confirmed (I was there) and Absent (I was not there), and the function's attendance total updates to match. A Checked-In row can only be changed in the desk, on the Function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "recur-h2-001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🔁Recurring Functions", "col": 12}}, {"id": "recur-desc-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A function can repeat on a schedule (for example, a weekly Bible Study). The function you set up is the template. Each day, Churchit makes the next occurrences of the template ahead of time, for the number of weeks in Create Weeks Ahead (8 weeks by default), so they show on the calendar early. Each occurrence copies the schedule, attendance roster, team needs, associations and other details of the template. It also copies the room bookings of the template that are Requested or Approved, moved to the new date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "recur-desc-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To make a Function repeat:
- Expand the Recurrence section and check Automatically Recreate.
- Choose a Repeat Frequency (Daily, Weekly, Monthly or Yearly). In Repeat Every, type 1 to repeat every time, or 2 to repeat every second day, week, month or year.
- For Weekly, choose the day in Repeat Day of Week.
- For Monthly, choose Repeat Monthly By. With Day of Month, type the day in Repeat Day of Month (for example, the 15th). A day after the end of a short month moves to the last day of that month. With Weekday, choose Repeat Week of Month and Repeat Day of Week (for example, the Second Sunday, or the Last Friday).
- Optionally set a Repeat Until date to stop making occurrences after that date.
- Add a date to Skip Dates when the function does not happen on that date (for example, a joint service). When you delete an occurrence, its room bookings are also deleted and its date is added to Skip Dates, so it is not made again.
- A changed rule applies only to the dates after the latest occurrence. To change occurrences that already exist, edit or delete them.
- If a room of the template is already booked at the new time, the occurrence is made without that booking, and a comment on the occurrence names the room and the time.
- A room that needs approval gets a booking with the status Requested, which waits for approval as usual.
- Uncheck Automatically Recreate at any time to stop making occurrences.
Tip: open a Ministry and click Create Recurring Function to start a new recurring function linked to that ministry. Each ministry's Recurring Functions list shows the recurring functions of the ministry.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "grp-meet-h3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "👥Group Meetings", "col": 12}}, {"id": "grp-meet-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Function can be a meeting of a Group. Choose the group in the Group field of the Function. Do not add a group in Associations: Churchit does not accept a new Group row there. The group must belong to the church of the Function, and a Function with a group cannot be shared with all churches. A Function that had a group in Associations before has it in Group now. When it had more than one group, a comment on the Function names the groups that stay in Associations.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "grp-meet-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To give a group a weekly or monthly meeting, open the group and click Actions → Set Up Meetings. A new Function opens with the group, the type Group Meeting and Automatically Recreate set. Choose the day, the time and the address, and save. This Function is the schedule of the group: Churchit makes each meeting from it, and each meeting keeps the group. Record the attendance on each meeting, not on the schedule.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "grp-meet-03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Did Not Meet. When a group did not meet, tick Did Not Meet on the Function of that meeting. Churchit then sends no attendance reminder for it, and the Group Attendance report does not count it. A leader can also do this on the Lead a Group page of the portal (see Lead a Group in the People manual). Attendance Recorded On shows when a leader last saved the attendance.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-h2-001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📝Function Sign-Ups", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-desc-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Function sign-ups allow people to indicate their intent to attend a function and optionally bring/complete specific items.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-desc-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating a sign-up, note the following:
- Only Functions that have Allow Sign-Ups ticked on the Registration tab are available in the 'Function' field.
- Each person can have only one sign-up per function. A Cancelled sign-up does not count.
- The Attending checkbox tells whether the person who signs up comes. While it is ticked, that person is in the Attendees table.
    - While the sign-up is Confirmed, each attendee Person has an attendance record on the Function with the status 'Signed-Up'. A record that says more, such as Checked-In, Confirmed or Absent, stays as it is.
    - When the sign-up stops being Confirmed, an attendee is removed, or the sign-up is deleted, Churchit removes the attendance record only while it is still 'Signed-Up'.
- If the Function has sign-up items defined, you can add rows to indicate which (and how many of those) items you will bring/complete.
    - The Signed Up quantity on each item in the Function document adds up the quantities of the sign-ups that hold seats (Confirmed, or Pending and not yet expired).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-h3-001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📦Sign-Up Items", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-item-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sign-up items represent things that are needed for a function (e.g. food, supplies, jobs, etc). They are added to a function's Sign-Up Items table with the quantity needed. As people submit sign-ups and indicate they will bring specific items, the Quantity Signed Up on the function is automatically totaled across all sign-ups and displayed on the Function document.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-reg-h3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🌐Guest Sign-Ups and the Register Page", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-guest-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A person who is not signed in can sign up for a function on the Register page of the website. To allow it, open the Function, tick Publish on the Details tab, and tick Allow Sign-Ups and Allow Guest Sign-Ups on the Registration tab. The Register page shows only published functions that start today or later. The Register page is not in the website menu. Put a link to /register on a web page, in an email or in a QR code. To add it to the menu, open Website Settings, add a row to Top Bar Items with the Label Register and the URL /register, and save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-guest-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A guest types a name and an email, and can add a phone number and notes. A signed-in member signs up as their own person. A guest's sign-up has no Person at first. A moment later Churchit links it to the one person whose name and email or phone match. If nobody matches, Churchit adds the guest as a Visitor with the Source Sign-Up, and records possible duplicates for staff. If the matched person is already signed up for the function, the new sign-up stays without a Person and gets a comment that names the other sign-up. A guest never sees the name of anyone else.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-bring-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Bringing others. On the Register page, a signed-in member can tick the people of their own household who come too. Anyone can click Add a person and type the name of someone else who comes. Each person takes a seat. When the function has selections, each person chooses one, and the registrant chooses their own. A registration can bring at most 20 other people.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-status-h3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🚦Status and Open and Close Dates", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-status-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each sign-up has a status: Pending, Confirmed, Waitlisted or Cancelled. Only Churchit sets it. To cancel a sign-up, open it and click Cancel Registration. A cancelled sign-up keeps its record, and the person can sign up again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-window-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On the Registration tab, Sign-Ups Open On and Sign-Ups Close On set when members and guests can sign up. Leave a date blank for no limit. Outside these dates, the members' sign-up form and the Register page do not offer the function, and a member can still cancel. Staff can add a sign-up in the desk at any time.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-seats-h3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🎟️Capacity, Waitlist and Approval", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-capacity-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Capacity on the Registration tab is the number of people who can come. Leave it at 0 for no limit. Add Selections when people choose an option, such as Adult or Child, and give each one a price and a capacity if it needs them. When a function has selections, each attendee must choose one. On a sign-up, the Attendees table lists the people who come. A sign-up that only brings items, with Attending unticked, takes no seat. In the Sign-Up Items table of the Function, tick Limited on an item to refuse sign-ups when its Quantity Needed is reached.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-waitlist-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Waitlist. When a capacity is full, a new sign-up gets the status Waitlisted, and the whole party waits together. A party that is larger than a capacity cannot sign up. When seats become free, Churchit gives them to the oldest waiting party that fits. Seats become free when a sign-up is cancelled, declined or deleted, when a party removes an attendee, when a payment hold ends, or when you raise a capacity. If you move a sign-up to another function, it counts as a new sign-up there. When that function is full, the sign-up is Waitlisted, and its seats in the first function go to the waitlist of that function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-approval-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Approval. Tick Sign-Ups Need Approval on the Registration tab to approve each sign-up yourself. A new sign-up is then Pending and keeps its seats until you decide. Open the sign-up and click Approval, then Approve or Decline. Only a Church Manager or a Church People Editor can approve or decline. An approved sign-up is Confirmed, or Pending with a payment hold when an amount is due. A declined sign-up is Cancelled, and its seats go to the waitlist. When an approved sign-up adds attendees or items, it is Pending again and waits for your approval.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-money-h3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "💲Prices, Discounts and Payments", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-price-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Prices. Give each Selection a price for each attendee, and give a Sign-Up Item a price for each one. Churchit works out the Amount Due of a sign-up on each save: the price of each attendee's selection, plus the price of each item times its quantity, less the discount. The registrant cannot change a price.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-discount-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Discounts. Add rows to Discounts on the Registration tab. A Code discount applies when the registrant types its code in Discount Code on the Register page. Capital letters do not matter. An Early Bird discount applies to sign-ups made on or before its Valid Until date. A Group discount applies when a sign-up brings at least its Minimum Attendees. Use it only on a function whose selections have a price. A Freely Given discount applies to every sign-up. Each row takes its Amount off, or its Percent when Amount is empty. A Valid Until date ends any discount after that day. When more than one discount applies, only the largest one comes off. The amount due is never below 0. Registrants never see the codes.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-freely-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Freely given. \"Freely you have received; freely give\" (Matthew 10:8). When a function has a price, its form asks you to consider giving it freely. Click Offer It Freely to add a Freely Given discount of 100 percent and save the function. Every sign-up is then free, sign-ups that wait for payment are confirmed, the Register page shows each price as freely given, and the function needs no Sign-Up Fund. With a Valid Until date the function is free only until that day, so it still needs a fund.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-pay-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Payments. When a function has a price and is not freely given, choose a Sign-Up Fund on the Registration tab. The fund must belong to the church of the function, or be shared. A sign-up with an amount due is Pending and holds its seats for 24 hours. The registrant gets an email with a Pay now link, and the Register page shows the link after they sign up. When the payment arrives, Churchit adds a Collection with one row for the fund and confirms the sign-up. The row has no person, so the payment is not on a giving statement. If the sign-up is not paid in 24 hours, Churchit cancels it and gives its seats to the waitlist. If your church offers no online payment method, the email asks the registrant to pay at the church office.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-pay-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Offline payments and refunds. When a person pays in cash or by check, open the sign-up and click Payment, then Record Offline Payment. Put the money in the weekly collection. If a payment arrives after the hold ended and the seats are gone, or a paid sign-up is cancelled or declined, the sign-up gets the payment status Refund Due and Church Finance gets an alert. Only a Church Manager can delete a paid sign-up. Refund the payment at the payment processor, then open the sign-up and click Payment, then Record Refund. Only Church Finance and Church Manager users can record payments and refunds. A paid sign-up cannot add anything that costs more, and cannot move to another function. Make a new sign-up instead.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-more-h3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "✉️Questions, Emails and Reports", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-questions-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Questions. To ask questions when people register, make a Question Set and choose it in Question Set on the Registration tab. A function can use a question set of its own church or a shared one. The Register page asks the questions once for the registrant and once for each person they bring. A required question must be answered for each person, or the registration is not saved. You see the answers in the Answers section of each sign-up and in the Function Registrations report. If you change the questions later, sign-ups made before keep their answers. Staff cannot type answers in the desk, and the members' sign-up form does not ask the questions. To add a sign-up for a function with required questions, use the Register page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-confirm-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Confirmation. When a sign-up becomes Confirmed, Churchit emails the registrant a confirmation with a calendar file of the function. It goes to the primary email of the person. A guest sign-up that has no person yet gets it at the email the guest typed. It is sent each time a sign-up becomes Confirmed: when it is confirmed, approved, paid or moved off the waitlist, again after it waited for payment or approval a second time, and when staff move it to another function. Pending and Waitlisted sign-ups get no confirmation. After a person registers, the Register page shows an Add to calendar link. To change the text, edit the Email Template Sign-Up Confirmation. To stop the email, delete that template. The Email Template Sign-Up Payment Due holds the text of the payment email. Churchit sends these emails only when the site has an outgoing email account.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-remind-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Reminders. Set Reminder Days on the Registration tab to the number of days before the function to send a reminder. 0 sends no reminder. Each day, the registrant of each Confirmed sign-up of a function that starts within Reminder Days gets one reminder by email. If the site can send texts, a registrant who agreed to texts for Event Registrations also gets one text. A registrant who withdrew consent for Event Registrations gets no reminder. The other attendees get no reminder. To change the words of the email, edit the Email Template Sign-Up Reminder.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-report-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Reports. The Function Registrations report shows one row for each person who comes, with the sign-up, their selection, the status and the payment. Choose a function to see a column for each of its questions with the answer of each person. You can also filter by status. The Function Sign-Up Items report shows the items, with the name a guest typed for a guest sign-up.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-shared-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "More than one church. A sign-up belongs to the church of its function. The sign-ups of a function that is shared with all churches are shared too, so every church sees them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qset-h2-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📋Question Sets", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qset-desc-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Question Set is a list of questions that your church asks people, for example when they register. The answers stay on the record that the person filled in, so you read them there.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qset-desc-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To make a Question Set, open Question Sets (in the Settings workspace, under Forms) and click Add Question Set. Give it a Title. Then add one row for each question:
- Question: the question as people read it, such as T-shirt size.
- Answer Type: a line of text (Data), a paragraph (Small Text), a choice from a list (Select), a tick (Check), a date, a whole number (Int), an email address or a phone number.
- Required: tick this when people must answer. A required tick must be ticked, for example to agree to the rules of a camp.
- Choices: for a Select question, type each choice on a new line.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qset-desc-03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each question gets an Answer Name, made from the question. Two questions in one set cannot have the same Answer Name. Do not change an Answer Name after people answer, because their answers are kept under it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qset-desc-04", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A question cannot depend on the answer to another question. To ask different people different questions, make a second Question Set.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qset-desc-05", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each answer keeps the question as it was asked, so a later change to the set does not change an old answer. A tick shows as Yes or No. A question that someone leaves blank shows no answer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qset-desc-06", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you anonymize a person, the answers on the records that are theirs are removed, with the change history of those records. Answers on a record for a group, where the person is only one of the people listed, stay. A function sign-up is different: the answers of the person are removed, and the answers of the other people on the sign-up stay. When you merge two people, the answers stay.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qset-desc-07", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In multi-church mode, a Question Set belongs to one church. Tick Shared with All Churches to let every church use it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "form-h3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📝Forms", "col": 12}}, {"id": "form-desc-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To use a Question Set as a form on the website, tick Publish as a Form. Anyone can then answer it at /form/new?question_set= followed by the name of the set, such as QSET-0001. Copy this address into a web page, an email or a QR code. The form asks for a first name, a last name and an email address, and then the questions of the set. When Publish as a Form is not ticked, the form says that it is not open.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "form-desc-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tick Members Only to let only signed-in members answer. A member's answer is linked to their own person record. Other people are asked to log in as a member.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "form-desc-03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each answer is a Form Response, in the Settings workspace under Forms. After a guest sends a form, Churchit finds the person who has the same name and email, or adds them as a Visitor with the Source Form. Then the response shows Processed. To follow up a form, add a trigger Form Submitted to a Follow-up Workflow and choose the Question Set. Each response to that set opens one card for the person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "form-desc-04", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Before you charge for a form, remember \"Freely you have received; freely give\" (Matthew 10:8): a form with no Price is free. To charge for a form, give the Question Set a Price and a Fund of its church or a shared one. After a person sends the form, they go to the payment page. When the payment arrives, Churchit adds a Collection with one row for the fund, and the response shows Paid. After you refund a payment at the payment processor, open the Form Response and click Record Refund. Only Church Finance and Church Manager users can do this.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "form-desc-05", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In multi-church mode, a response belongs to the church of its Question Set. A response to a shared Question Set is shared too, so every church sees it, and the own church of the person follows it up.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h2-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🙋Ministry Teams", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-desc-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A ministry team is the people who serve in a ministry, such as greeters, ushers or nursery workers. Churchit asks each person by email, or by text, if they can serve at a function, and keeps their answer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🧩Positions", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-pos-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Ministry Team Position is one job on a ministry's team (e.g. Greeter in the Hospitality ministry).
- Add the people who can fill the position under People. Only these people can be assigned to it.
- Check Needs Background Check when the position needs a current, cleared Background Check (e.g. Nursery Worker).
- Under Required Checks, pick the checks the position needs, for example Criminal Background and Child Safety Training. Each one must be cleared and still current on the day of the function. Leave it blank to accept any cleared check.
- Tick Block People Without Checks to refuse an assignment for someone without the checks. Without it, you only get a warning.
- When you add someone to the position's People who does not have the checks, you get a warning, but they stay on the list.
- Each row of People has Most Times a Month. 0 means no limit. When a person already has this many Pending or Accepted assignments to the position in the month of a function, a new assignment shows a warning. Members set this number themselves on the Ministry Team page, under How often you serve.
- On the Ministry, set the Team Coordinator, who gets an email when someone declines, and Remind Days Before: how many days before a function the people serving get a reminder. 0 sends no reminders. The ministry's positions show under Connections.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📋Team Needs and Assignments", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-need-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On a Function, list the positions it needs, and how many people each needs, in the Ministry Team section. Recurring functions and Fill from Template copy these needs from the template. Notes on a need is a note to the people in that position. Each person sees only the note of their own position, on the Ministry Team page.
To ask a person to serve, make a Ministry Team Assignment from the Connections of the function: choose the position and the person. A warning shows when:
- a Ministry Team Block covers the date of the function, also a block that repeats
- the person already serves at another function at the same time
- the position needs a background check and the person has no current, cleared one
- the person already has their Most Times a Month for the position
- the person has no email address
A warning does not stop the save. The function, position and person cannot change after the save: delete the assignment and make a new one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-fill-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Fill Open Needs. To ask people to fill the open places of a function, click Ministry Team → Fill Open Needs on the Function. The Ministry Team Schedule and Ministry Team Grid reports have a Fill Open Needs button too. It fills every function in the dates, church and ministry of the filters.
- For each position, it takes people from the People of the position. It asks first the person who served longest ago, or never.
- It does not ask a person who is blocked on that date, who serves at the same time, who does not have a check the position needs, who already has their Most Times a Month, or who has died. It asks a person for one position of a function only.
- It does not ask a person again for a place they were already asked about, also when they declined.
- Each new assignment is Pending, and the daily job sends the requests. After a person declines, click it again to fill the place.
- It does not fill a function that has started.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "✉️Emails and Answers", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-email-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Once a day, each person gets one email that lists their new assignments. To send the waiting emails at once, click Send Requests Now on the Ministry Team Assignment list. Each assignment has a link to accept or decline it, with an optional reason. The link works without signing in. Members can also answer on the Ministry Team page of the portal, where they see the Schedule of each function they serve at. While they have not declined, the schedule also shows the key and arrangement of each song, the team notes, the note for their own position and the rehearsal media of the songs. A person can change their answer until the function starts.
- The Status of the assignment shows the answer: Pending, Accepted or Declined.
- When someone declines, the Team Coordinator of the ministry gets an email, and the place is open again in the schedule.
- A reminder goes out the ministry's Remind Days Before ahead of the function, to each person who has not declined.
- No email goes out until the site has an outgoing Email Account. Change the words of the four emails in Email Templates: Ministry Team Request, Ministry Team Reminder, Ministry Team Decline and Ministry Team Replacement.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-text-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Texts. If your site can send texts (a gateway in SMS Settings), each request and reminder also goes by text. A person gets the text only when they gave text consent for the Serving purpose. The text has the link to accept or decline. The emails go as before, to everyone asked to serve, when the site has an outgoing Email Account. If the site can send only texts, the requests still go by text. When you click Send Requests Now and none of your roles is in the Allowed Roles of SMS Settings, Churchit sends nothing to the people who get texts. The daily job sends them the email and the text.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-email-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To write to everyone serving at a function, click Ministry Team → Email the Team on the Function. The email goes to each person asked to serve who has not declined. They are in BCC, so no one sees the others' email addresses. The email is kept on the function's timeline, and a message names anyone without an email address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-replace", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🔄Replacement Requests", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-replace-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A volunteer who cannot come can ask someone else to take their place. On the Ministry Team page, or on the page that the request email links to, they click Ask Someone Else and choose a person. The list shows only the people of the position who are free then: no block, no other assignment at the same time, the checks the position needs, and not at their Most Times a Month. People already asked for this place are not on the list.
- The person they choose gets a request at once. The volunteer still serves until that person accepts. A volunteer can have only one request waiting at a time.
- When the person accepts, the volunteer's assignment changes to Declined with the reason Replaced by and the name, and the Team Coordinator gets the decline email, which names the person who takes the place.
- When the person declines, nothing changes for the volunteer, and the Team Coordinator gets no email.
- Either way, the volunteer gets the Ministry Team Replacement email.
- The Replaces field of the new assignment shows which assignment it replaces. You cannot set it by hand.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-cal", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📅Calendar", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-cal-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members can see the functions they accepted in the calendar on their phone or computer. On the Ministry Team page of the portal, they click Make a calendar link, then Subscribe, or copy the link into their calendar app (in Google Calendar: Other calendars, From URL). The calendar keeps itself up to date.
Anyone with the link can see where the member serves. Stop this link and make a new one replaces a link that was shared by mistake.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-04", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🚫Blocked Dates", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-block-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Ministry Team Block holds the dates a person cannot serve, such as a vacation. Check Whole Household to block everyone in their family. Members add and remove their own blocks on the Ministry Team page of the portal. On a site with branch churches, only the person's own church can add a Ministry Team Block for them. Staff at another church ask that church, or the person adds the block on the Ministry Team page.
Repeating blocks. A block can repeat. Set Repeat to Weekly, Every Other Week or Monthly on the Same Weekday. Monthly uses the weekday and the week of the month of From Date, for example the first Sunday. A block that starts on a fifth Sunday covers only the months that have a fifth Sunday. The dates from From Date to To Date repeat until Repeat Until. Leave Repeat Until empty to repeat with no end. A repeating block must end before it repeats: for example, a weekly block can be at most 7 days long. On the Ministry Team page, members choose Repeat and an optional Repeat until date when they add a block. Blocks only warn. They do not stop an assignment.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-05", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🗓️Ministry Team Schedule", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-report-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Ministry Team Schedule report shows the positions of each function in a date range: how many people each needs, how many accepted or did not answer yet, how many places are open, and who was asked. Check Only Open Positions to see the gaps. On a Function, Ministry Team → Schedule opens the report for that function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-grid-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Ministry Team Grid report shows several weeks at once: one row for each position, grouped by ministry, and one column for each function that has team needs or assignments. Each cell shows the open places in red and the people asked: green for Accepted, orange for Pending and gray for Declined. Click an open place to make an assignment for that function and position. The grid shows 8 weeks by default, and at most 60 functions. For a longer range, choose shorter dates.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-served-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each person's Last Served and Times Served (90 Days), on the Connections tab of the Person form, count the functions where they accepted an assignment. Pending and declined requests do not count. Filter the Person list on them to find, for example, people who have not served lately.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h2-001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "✅Function Check-Ins", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-desc-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Function check-ins are a record that a person has physically arrived at a function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-desc-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating a check-in, note the following:
- Each person can only be checked in once per function.
- Each check-in has a Kind: Regular, Guest or Volunteer. A visitor added at the Check-In Station is a Guest. A Volunteer check-in gets no security code, does not count in the room capacity and does not start a First Check-In follow-up card. The attendance row is Checked-In for every kind.
- Upon saving, the person's attendance record on the function will automatically be set to Checked-In.
- Deleting a check-in will remove the associated Checked-In attendance record from the function. A check-in of a person who was checked out or collected cannot be deleted.
- The Kind cannot be changed after the check-in is saved.
- The checkout fields (Collected By, Collected At, Released By, Override Reason, Overridden By and the Security Code) are set only at the Check-In Station. A check-in created here gets no security code, so use the Check-In Station for children who need a pickup tag.
- When 'Room Capacity' in Check-In Settings is Block, a check-in created here is refused when the room is full.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h3-station", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🖥️Check-In Station", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-station-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Check-In Station is the quickest way to check people in as they arrive:
1. Choose the Function at the top of the page. The station remembers the last function used on that computer and otherwise picks the next function on the calendar. The arrow in the field (or the function name above the Checked In list) opens the Function itself.
2. Type part of a name, a nickname, a family name, or a phone number. Results are grouped by family so parents and children can be checked in together. People who have a 'Death' life event are not listed.
3. Tap the people who have arrived (or Select all for a family) and click Check In. Pressing Enter checks in a single match straight away.
4. First-time visitors: click New Visitor (or the Add them as a new visitor link when a search finds no one), confirm the name and phone taken from what you typed, and click Add & Check In. Churchit first looks for people who are already in Churchit with the same name and phone number (see New Visitors below). A new visitor is created and checked in as a Guest. Their 'Source' is Check-In and their 'Membership' is Visitor, so the member directory does not list them.
The Checked In list on the right shows everyone at the function (see below). Untick Print name tags to check people in without printing.
The station is also reachable from the Check-In Station button on any Function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-care-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Grade, allergies and medical notes. Each person in the search results shows their age, their grade and, in red, their allergies. A stethoscope icon shows that the person has medical notes or an emergency contact. Tap the icon to read them. The tap does not select the person. Only users who can see Medical Notes on the Person (Church Check-In, Church People Editor and Church Manager) see the icon.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-visitor-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "New Visitors. When you add a new visitor, the station first looks for people who are already in Churchit with the same first and last name, or with a similar name and the same phone number. If it finds someone, it shows them with their family and age. Click Check In next to the right person to check them in as a Guest. No new person is added. Click Add as New Visitor to add a new person. Type the phone number too: it helps the station find a person whose name is spelled differently. A visitor who has no household adult in Churchit, such as a visiting child, can have an emergency contact: open Emergency Contact in the New Visitor window and type the name and phone number.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-roster-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Checked In list. The list on the right shows everyone checked in to the function, newest first, with their photo. It updates every 10 seconds while the page is open, so you also see the check-ins and checkouts of other stations. It stops when the browser tab is hidden or you go to another page. Each row shows In, Collected by the person who collected the child, or Checked out, with the time. The names of the booked rooms show under the function name. They come from the approved Room Bookings of the function. To find a person, type part of a name or a security code in Filter by name or code. The buttons on a row reprint the name tag, undo the check-in, check the person out and page the parents. After a person is checked out or collected, only the reprint button stays.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-checkout-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Check Out. To record that a person without a pickup tag has left, such as an adult or a volunteer, click the exit button on their row, then click Yes. The Function Check-In then shows when they left and who checked them out. A child with a pickup tag leaves only through Verify Pickup. A check-in that is checked out or collected cannot be undone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-page-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Page Parents. To ask the parents of a child to come, click the bell on the child's row in the Checked In list, then click Yes. Churchit sends a short message to each Adult of the child's household. An Adult who agreed to texts for the Child Safety purpose gets a text. The other Adults get an email. An Adult that a Pickup Restriction names for the child gets nothing. The station then shows the names of the parents it reached. Each message shows on the timeline of the child and of the parent. If the station shows No parent reached, send a runner to find the parents. You can page the parents of one child only once in 2 minutes. You cannot page the parents of a child who was collected.
Texts go only when SMS Settings has a gateway and the Church Check-In role is in its Allowed Roles. Otherwise the station sends emails only. Emails need an outgoing Email Account. A parent agrees to texts on the Communication Preferences page of the portal, or staff record a Communication Consent for Child Safety.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-headcount-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Headcount. Some people in a room do not check in by name. To count them, type the number of people in the room in the Headcount box under Checked In, then click Save or press Enter. The attendance total of the function is the larger of the headcount and the number of people counted by name. The box shows only for a function that has started. A headcount cannot be negative. To clear it, empty the box and click Save. You can also change 'Headcount' on the Function form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-team-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Team. The Team tab lists the people who accepted a Ministry Team position at the function, with their position. Click Check In next to a name to check that person in as a Volunteer. A volunteer gets no security code and no pickup tag. Their name tag shows the word Volunteer and their position. People with a Pending or Declined assignment are not listed.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-limits-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Age and grade limits. In the Age and Grade section of a Function, you can set 'Minimum Age', 'Maximum Age', 'Minimum Grade' and 'Maximum Grade'. The limits use the age and grade of the person on the start date of the function. A person with no birth date does not pass an age limit, and a person with no graduation year does not pass a grade limit. At the Check-In Station, if a person is outside a limit, a window shows the name and the reason. Click Yes to check in the person, or No to stop. A Volunteer check-in has no limit check. A self check-in kiosk and a pre check-in code do not offer the function to a person outside its limits. A function that repeats gives its limits to each new occurrence.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-capacity-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Room capacity. The capacity of a function is the total 'Capacity' of the rooms in its approved Room Bookings. If the function has no approved booking, or the rooms have no capacity, there is no limit. The people in the room are the people who are checked in and not collected or checked out. Volunteers are not counted. Set 'Room Capacity' in Check-In Settings:
- Off: no capacity check.
- Warn (the default): the check-in is saved, and the station shows an orange warning when the room has more people than its capacity.
- Block: the station, the kiosk, pre check-in and the Function Check-In form do not check people in when the room has no place for them. When a child is collected, a place opens again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-scan-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Scan Card. A person can show their Member QR Card instead of saying their name. Click Scan Card next to the search box and hold the card in front of the camera. The station shows the person and their family, as a name search does. Tap the people who arrived and click Check In, or press Enter to check in only the card holder. If the station cannot find the person, it shows \"No one found for this card\". The camera works only on a site that uses https. The station finds the same people as a name search. If your church keeps people private, a card from another church finds no one, except at a Function that is shared with all churches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h3-pickup", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🧒Verify Pickup", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-pickup-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use Verify Pickup when an adult comes to collect a child. It works only when Print Security Codes is ticked in Check-In Settings, because the code comes from the pickup tag. A household keeps one code for the whole day: if a family checks in a second child later, or at another function on the same day, the new tag has the same code. No two households have the same code on one day.
1. Click Verify Pickup at the top of the Check-In Station.
2. Type the 4 characters of the security code on the adult's pickup tag. Press Enter or click Verify. The pickup tag also has a QR code of the security code: click Scan and hold the tag in front of the camera to fill in the code.
3. The station shows each person who was checked in with this code today, with their photo and the Function. Below them, it shows who may collect them: the Adults of the household and the family's Authorized Pickups, with their photos, relationship and notes. Below them, it shows the Pickup Restrictions of the children in red: who may not collect which child, what to do, and until when. A restricted Adult also shows 'Restricted from collecting' with the child's name.
4. Compare the adult at the desk with these people. Release the child only to one of them. Do not release a child to a restricted person: the station refuses. A Church Manager can release the child to them. The station then asks for the reason and records it on the Function Check-In with the manager's name.
5. Keep a tick beside each child the adult is taking, and click Release beside the adult. Churchit records on each child's Function Check-In who collected them, when, and which volunteer released them. The station then shows \"Collected by\" with the time, and the child cannot be released again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-pickup-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If the station shows No child is checked in with this code today, do not release the child. Ask a member of staff. A code from an earlier day does not work. If the station shows two families, ask for the child's name.
To see who collected the children of a function, open the Function Check-In list and add the Collected By and Collected At columns. Only people the station shows can be released; for anyone else, ask a member of staff.
With more than one church, the station finds only the check-ins of Functions in your church and of Functions that are shared with all churches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h3-tags", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🏷️Name Tags", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-tags-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A name tag prints for every check-in made at the station. Name tags can also be printed from a Function Check-In (Print Name Tag), for several check-ins from the Function Check-In list (Actions → Print Name Tags), or for any people without a check-in from the Person list (Actions → Print Name Tags).
Tags are Print Formats on Function Check-In: Name Tag (used for browser printing) and Zebra Name Tag (ZPL, used for Zebra printers). To change the layout, duplicate the standard format, edit the copy, and select it in Check-In Settings.
Tick Print Security Codes in Check-In Settings for children's ministry: everyone in one household gets the same random four-character code on their tag for the whole day, and one extra Pickup tag listing their names and the code prints for the adult who collects them. The code is stored on each Function Check-In. A Volunteer check-in gets no code and no pickup tag. The pickup tag has a QR code of the security code, which Verify Pickup can scan.
Name tags print the person's Nickname when they have one, and their first name when they do not. The pickup tag lists the same names.
Tick Print Allergies on Name Tags in Check-In Settings to print a person's allergies under their name, taken from the 'Allergies' field on the Person. Tags for people with no allergies are unchanged, and pickup tags never show allergies.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-tags-kind-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A tag for each kind of check-in. Use Tag Formats by Kind in Check-In Settings to print a different name tag for Regular, Guest or Volunteer check-ins. Add one row for each kind. A kind with no row uses the Name Tag Format and ZPL Format above. A row with no ZPL format prints the default ZPL format on Zebra printers. New sites start with a Volunteer row that uses the Volunteer Name Tag format, which prints the word Volunteer, the name and the position. Pickup tags always use the formats above.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h3-printers", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🖨️Label Printer Setup", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-printers-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Choose how tags reach the printer under Name Tag Printing in Check-In Settings, set the label size (4 × 2 in is the common Zebra name tag, 2.25 × 1.25 in the common Dymo one), then use Print Test Tag:
- Browser: works with any printer that has a driver installed (Zebra, Dymo, Brother, an office printer). The browser's print dialog opens for each batch; pick the label printer and the label paper size once and the browser remembers it. To skip the dialog on a dedicated check-in computer, start Chrome with the --kiosk-printing flag and set the label printer as the computer's default printer.
- Zebra Browser Print: silent printing to a Zebra printer (e.g. ZD421) connected by USB or network to the station computer. Install Zebra's free Browser Print app on that computer, set the printer as its default, and accept this site when the app asks. Set Printer DPI to match the printer (203 or 300).
- QZ Tray: silent printing to any printer the station computer can see, sending ZPL. Install the free QZ Tray app and, if the label printer is not the default, enter its name under Printer Name. QZ Tray asks once to allow this site.
- Network Printer: no software on the station computer at all. Enter the IP address of a Zebra printer that is on the same network as the Churchit server (port 9100). The server sends the labels straight to the printer, so this needs a self-hosted server on the church network.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fciPrinterChurch1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "More than one church. Each campus usually has its own label printer, so add a row under Printers Per Church in Check-In Settings for any church that prints somewhere else. Fill in only what differs: anything left blank in the row uses the settings above it. A station always prints to its operator's own church's printer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h3-kiosk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📱Self Check-In Kiosk", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-kiosk-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A self check-in kiosk lets families check themselves in on a tablet or a computer at the door. It shows only today's functions whose Function Type has 'Allow Self Check-In' ticked, from a number of minutes before the start ('Self Check-In Opens (Minutes Before Start)' in Check-In Settings, 60 by default) to the end.
To set up a kiosk:
1. Add a User for the kiosk device, with the role Church Check-In Kiosk and no other role. In multi-church mode, give it exactly one Church User Permission, for the church it serves. With none or more than one, the kiosk refuses to work. In 'Restrict IP', type the address of your church network, so the login works only at church.
2. In each Function Type that families may check in to by themselves, tick 'Allow Self Check-In'.
3. On the kiosk device, open /check-in-kiosk and sign in as the kiosk user. Leave the page open.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-kiosk-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A family types its whole phone number, as the church office keeps it (with the country code if the record has one). The kiosk shows the people of that household who may check in now, with their photo and grade. A child outside the age or grade limits of a function is not offered that function. The family ticks who to check in, picks a function when there is more than one, and taps Check In. The name tags print through the printer settings of the kiosk's church. The kiosk prints tags only for new check-ins. When the household already has a pickup code today, for example a child was checked in at the Check-In Station, the kiosk prints the name tags without the code and no pickup tag: use the pickup tag from earlier. For a new tag, go to the Check-In Station. In Block mode, a full room refuses the check-in.
The kiosk cannot add visitors, check people out or read any record. Children leave through Verify Pickup at the Check-In Station. For printing with the browser, start Chrome with --kiosk-printing so the tags print without a dialog. QZ Tray does not work on the kiosk page. Use Browser, Zebra Browser Print or a network printer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h3-precheckin", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📲Pre Check-In", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-precheckin-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members can check in before they arrive. On the My Household page of the portal, a member sees Check In Before You Arrive when one of today's functions of their church allows self check-in and check-in is open. The member ticks the people who come, picks the function and taps Get Check-In Code. A member can choose only themselves and the Children they may edit. A person outside the age or grade limits of the function cannot be chosen.
At the church, scan the code. At the Check-In Station, click Scan Card and hold the code in front of the camera: the people are checked in to the function of the code, and their name tags print when Print name tags is ticked. At a self check-in kiosk, scan the code with a handheld scanner that types into the phone number field. The kiosk checks people in only to its own church's functions.
The code works only until the function ends, and only while check-in is open. A changed code does nothing. A second scan of the same code checks in nobody new and prints no tags.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KbmdGnFK8k", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Bulk Check-In from the Person list
1. Open the Person list view.
2. Select (Check) the people you would like to check-in.
3. Click `Actions -> Check In`
4. Choose which Function for which you would like to check the people in.
The people's attendance will be tracked in the Function document.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bLMhfdXsV3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🎵Songs", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7ts41_VmsH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Songs can be added as items to a church function.
To show a song on a screen, open the song and click Present. You can also add the song as a slide to a sermon and leave its fields empty: the presentation then shows each slide of the song.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ljVNwCikn3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you create a song, note the following:
- If you know the CCLI number of the song, add it. The Song Usage report shows it.
- Authors: the writers of the words and the music.
- Copyright: the copyright line of the song, as the publisher gives it.
- Tick Public Domain only when the words and the music are free of copyright. Visitors who are not signed in see the words of a song only when Public Domain is ticked. For any other song they see 'This slide is not public'.
- Default Key: the key that the team usually plays the song in. Tempo (BPM) is the speed in beats per minute. Time Signature is for example 4/4 or 6/8.
- Themes: add tags to the song in the sidebar of the form, for example Advent or Easter. To find the songs of a theme, filter the Song list by the tag.
- You can add any number of slides to a song.
- The last slide of a song shows its copyright and its CCLI number with your church's CCLI License Number. Add the license number on your church. It is the number of your CCLI Church Copyright License.
- After you create a song, you can add it to the Schedule of a function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "song-arr-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Arrangements. An arrangement is one way that the team plays a song. Each arrangement has a name, a key, a tempo, notes and a ChordPro chart. Two arrangements of one song cannot have the same name. In a ChordPro chart, put each chord in square brackets before the syllable that you sing on it, for example [G]Amazing [D/F#]grace. Start a section with a line such as Verse 1 or Chorus, or put it between {start_of_verse} and {end_of_verse}. Leave a blank line between sections.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "song-chart-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Chord Chart. Save the song, then click Chord Chart. Select an arrangement and a key. The chart shows each chord above its words. When you select a different key, Churchit moves every chord to that key, with the sharps or flats of the key. A chart in a major key moves only to major keys, and a chart in a minor key only to minor keys. To change the key, the arrangement or the song must have a key. Church Staff can open the chord chart.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "song-slides-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Make Slides from ChordPro. Click Make Slides from ChordPro and select an arrangement. Churchit makes one slide for each section of the chart, with the words and no chords. This replaces all the slides of the song, so Churchit asks you first. The chart is the source of the slides: when you change the chart, make the slides again. Only a user who can edit the song can make slides.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "song-media-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Rehearsal media. Add chord charts, lead sheets, audio and video in the Media table. Attach a file or type a link. When you set Arrangement, it must be the name of an arrangement of the song. Leave it empty when the media is for every arrangement. The people who serve at a function see the media of each song on its schedule on their Ministry Team page, until the function ends. A media link that they saved works until 7 days after the function. They do not see the media when they declined, and they cannot open the songs themselves. Churchit makes one song for each file, with an arrangement named Default and one slide for each section. It copies the title, the CCLI number, the authors, the copyright, the key and the tempo. The themes of the file become tags. A SongSelect .usr file has no chords, so its Default arrangement holds only the words. When your list already shows a song with the same CCLI number, or the same title when the file has no CCLI number, Churchit skips the file. A song of another church that is not shared does not count. After the import, Churchit shows the songs it made and the files it skipped. Churchit then deletes the uploaded files. Select the hymns you want and click Add. Churchit makes one song for each hymn, with Public Domain ticked, an arrangement named Default with the chord chart, and one slide for each verse and chorus.
